rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for wording, tone, or style that sounds like familiar conversation rather than formal writing.

example.english: This notice was made more colloquial, so it sounds less stiff.
example.traditional: 呢段公告改到口語化啲，讀落冇咁生硬。
example.jyutping: ne1 dyun6 gung1 gou3 goi2 dou3 hau2 jyu5 faa3 di1 duk6 lok6 mou5 gam3 saang1 ngaang6

rows.note: Use this when describing language or an expression specifically as spoken-language usage, often before another noun such as 講法 or 表達.

example.english: “Thanks a lot” is a very common colloquial expression.
example.traditional: 「唔該晒」係好常見嘅口語講法。
example.jyutping: m4 goi1 saai3 hai6 hou2 soeng4 gin3 ge3 hau2 jyu5 gong2 faat3

rows.note: Choose this when the emphasis is on an informal, non-formal tone, without necessarily meaning that the wording specifically resembles speech.

example.english: The wording of this message is colloquial and feels quite friendly.
example.traditional: 呢封短訊用詞唔正式，幾有親切感。
example.jyutping: ni1 fung1 dyun2 seon3 jung6 ci4 m4 zing3 sik1 gei2 jau5 can1 cit3 gam2
